# Rebuild the integration branch

## Intent

A team that carries its own patches on top of a project it does not control needs one branch that always equals "the upstream project plus every patch that still applies, in order". The hub recomputes that branch, the integration branch, in a rebuild: it works out of sight of every client, tells the team which patch stopped applying and why, reuses conflict resolutions it has seen before, and replaces the branch in one step, so that a reader sees either the old branch or the new one and never a half-built one.

## Goals

- One attempt of a rebuild job fetches upstream, takes the patch list and the tips of the patch branches as they are at that moment, and builds the new integration head from those alone.
- Both strategies work: `rebase` replays the commits of each patch, `merge` merges each patch tip with a merge commit.
- A patch that conflicts is reported with a conflict report in the shape landing uses, and the run stops (`fail_fast`) or goes on without it (`continue`).
- Remembered resolutions are replayed before a conflict is reported, and learned from the patch branch.
- The integration branch moves once, by compare-and-swap, together with the changes of the patch list that belong to it.
- The job record shows progress after every patch and the full result at the end; every outcome emits its event.
- A rebuild that worked on inputs that have changed since queues one follow-up rebuild.
- The integration branch is pushed to origin after the publish when the workspace asks for it.

## Non-goals

- The durable job model, retries with backoff, dedup, crash recovery, the worker pool, the rebuild job record's storage and the routes and commands that submit, list, read, cancel and requeue a rebuild (§10.3.4, CP-FR-034 to CP-FR-039, CP-FR-056 to CP-FR-059): package 33 rebuild_jobs. This package is the handler those jobs run.
- Creating a carry-patch workspace, the upstream set-up, and adding and reading patches (CP-FR-001 to CP-FR-018): package 31 carry_patch_setup_and_patches.
- Updating, removing, restoring, reordering and resetting patches through the API (CP-FR-019 to CP-FR-033): package 32 patch_maintenance.
- Rollback of the integration branch and the rebuild preview (CP-FR-060 to CP-FR-066): package 35 rebuild_rollback_and_preview.
- The carry-patch part of sync, merge detection and the rebuild queued after a sync (CP-FR-067 to CP-FR-076): package 36 carry_patch_sync. This package only skips a patch that is already `merged_upstream` and removes it at the publish.
- Push control on the integration branch and on patch branches, the mirror of patch branches, and the rebuild trigger after a patch branch update (CP-FR-077 to CP-FR-088): package 37 carry_patch_push_control.
- Listing and forgetting remembered resolutions, the patch-status summary, the purge of deleted patches, and the discard of an interrupted rebuild's leftovers at start and the git safety rules (CP-FR-089 to CP-FR-097): package 38 carry_patch_rerere_and_maintenance. This package records the entries that package lists, in the transactional store, and exports the operation that discards scratch working trees. Crash recovery of jobs and the shutdown grace are package 33's.
- The conflict report's file entries and kinds (§8.3.3): package 26 conflict_reports_and_resolution. This package fills the report's rebuild-specific members and takes the file entries from that component.
- The event log itself: package 52 durable_event_log_and_stream.

## Background

The repository holds no code yet; every file named here is new. The source is `docs/prd/10_carry_patch.md`, requirements CP-FR-040 to CP-FR-055, with the data model of §10.3.2 (refs), §10.3.3 (patch), §10.3.5 (job record and patch result), §10.3.6 (conflict report) and §10.3.7 (remembered resolutions), the events of §10.8 and the configuration of §10.9.

The rebuild lives in `internal/carrypatch/`. It runs git through `internal/gitrepo/`, is called by the durable queue of `internal/jobs/` (package 33), emits events through `internal/event/` (package 52), and is wired into the process by `internal/hub/` (package 03). A workspace's bare repository is at `<[workspace].path>/<slug>.git` (package 10).

A rebuild job is created by package 33 with `strategy`, `fail_mode` and `integration_branch` captured when it was queued. A worker claims it and calls the handler of this package once per attempt.

## Requirements

### Starting an attempt (CP-FR-040, CP-FR-045, CP-FR-053, CP-FR-054)

An attempt first reads the workspace. If it is `archived` or `failed` the attempt ends as a permanent failure (reasons `workspace_archived`, `workspace_not_ready`) and the job is dead-lettered without retry. If it is `pending` or `cloning` the attempt ends as a retryable failure (reason `workspace_busy`). If the workspace no longer exists, its jobs were removed with it: the attempt ends without writing anything and without an event.

The same test is made again before every patch and inside the publish. A rebuild never blocks an archive, a reclone or a delete; when one happens during a run, the attempt ends at its next step in the way just described, and it has published nothing.

On a `ready` workspace the attempt fetches upstream with the upstream credentials (`UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT`, else `UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME` with `UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD`, else the origin credentials of the workspace) into `refs/remotes/upstream/*`, without tags, and resolves the **upstream base**: the head of the upstream's default branch, or, when that is unknown, the upstream branch named like the workspace's `default_branch`. The base is stored on the job as `upstream_head_sha`. A fetch that fails is a retryable failure (reason `upstream_fetch_failed`); so is a base that does not resolve (reason `upstream_unknown`). In both cases no patch is touched and nothing is published.

Each attempt starts with an empty `patch_results`.

### The patch list of a run (CP-FR-041, CP-FR-046, CP-FR-047)

After the fetch, the run lists the non-deleted patches in position order and records the present tip of each patch branch as `source_sha` (`null` when the branch does not exist). Only these recorded commits are used from then on. A push to a patch branch during the run is accepted as at any other time (no lock, CP-FR-053) and does not change what the run builds.

Patches are taken in position order:

- `disabled` and `merged_upstream` patches are `skipped` with that reason;
- a patch whose branch does not exist is `skipped` with `branch_not_found`;
- `active` and `conflict` patches are applied. A `conflict` patch is tried again by every rebuild.

After every patch the results so far are stored on the job, so that a read of a running job shows progress. A patch result has `patch_id`, `branch_name` and `position` as listed at the start, `status` (`success`, `conflict`, `skipped`), `skipped_reason` (`null` unless skipped), `source_sha`, `new_head_sha` (`null` unless `success`), `conflict_files` (`[]` unless `conflict`) and `conflict` (`null` unless `conflict`). The four counts of the job stay 0 until the job is `completed`.

### Building the new head (CP-FR-042, CP-FR-043)

The new head is built in a scratch working tree that no ref points to. Until the publish, no ref a client can read changes except `refs/remotes/upstream/*`.

The head under construction starts at the upstream base.

With strategy `rebase`, the commits of the patch are those reachable from `source_sha` and not from the upstream base, oldest first. Merge commits are left out. Each remaining commit is replayed onto the head under construction with its author, author date and message; the committer is the hub's landing identity (`[land].committer_name`, `[land].committer_email`, default `Parley <parley@localhost>`), never the process environment. A commit whose change is already present in the head under construction (from upstream or from an earlier patch) is dropped. A patch with no commit left to replay is `skipped` with `nothing_to_apply`.

With strategy `merge`, the patch tip is merged into the head under construction with a merge commit, even when a fast-forward is possible. The message is `Merge branch '<branch_name>'`; the first parent is the head under construction and the second is `source_sha`; author and committer are the hub's landing identity. A tip that is already reachable from the head under construction is `skipped` with `nothing_to_apply`.

A patch that applies is `success` and `new_head_sha` is the head under construction after it.

### Conflicts and fail modes (CP-FR-044, §10.3.6)

When a commit (or, with `merge`, the tip) does not apply, the hub first replays remembered resolutions (next section). If no path is left in conflict the patch goes on as if it had applied.

Otherwise the patch is undone: the head under construction returns to what it was before the patch. The patch's status becomes `conflict` and its `conflict_files` are set to the paths left in conflict, ordered by path; when the status changed, `parley.patch.update` is emitted with actor `system`, `changed: ["status"]`, `from`, `to: "conflict"` and `reason: "rebuild_conflict"`. The patch result is `conflict` with the same `conflict_files` and a conflict report:

| Member | Value |
|---|---|
| `patch_id` | the patch |
| `target_sha` | the head under construction before the patch: the upstream base for the first applied patch |
| `head_sha` | the patch's `source_sha` |
| `base_sha` | the merge base of `source_sha` and `target_sha` |
| `commit_sha` | `rebase`: the first commit that did not apply; `merge`: `source_sha` |
| `files` | one entry per path still in conflict after remembered resolutions were replayed, with `path`, `kind`, `base`, `ours` (the state under construction), `theirs` (the patch) and `landed_by: []` |
| `landed_changes` | `[]` |
| `change` | `null` |

Then:

- `fail_fast`: the run stops. Nothing is published. The attempt is a permanent failure with reason `conflict`: the job is `dead_letter`, its `conflict` is the report, its `error` names the patch branch, and it is not retried. `patch_results` ends with the conflicting patch.
- `continue`: the run goes on with the next patch from the state before the conflicting patch, and the integration branch is published without it.

A git failure that is not a conflict (reason `git_error`), a single git operation that runs longer than 10 minutes (reason `timeout`, CP-FR-093) and a shutdown of the hub (reason `shutdown`) are retryable failures. They are never recorded as a skip, a conflict or a success, they change no patch and they publish nothing.

### Remembered resolutions (CP-FR-044, §10.3.7)

Resolutions are remembered per workspace with git rerere, in the workspace's repository. When a commit does not apply, git replays every recorded resolution that matches a conflict of that commit. A path whose conflict is resolved this way is no longer in conflict.

For every conflict git records during a run, the hub keeps an entry: the id git gave the conflict, the path it was in, whether a resolution is recorded, and `recorded_at` (the time of the conflict while unresolved, the time of the resolution afterwards). Package 38 lists and forgets these entries.

A resolution is learned from the patch branch. When paths are left in conflict and the patch has two-parent merge commits among the commits the upstream base lacks, the hub redoes each of those merges (the newest 50 at most) in the scratch working tree. Where a redone merge conflicts, the content the merge commit has for the conflicted files is the developer's resolution, and git records it for that conflict. The hub then tries the commit that did not apply once more. This is how "a later rebuild sees the same conflict resolved": a developer who merges upstream into the patch branch and resolves the conflict there has taught the hub, and every later rebuild that meets the same conflict applies the patch without help.

A workspace's resolutions are never replayed in another workspace.

### Publish (CP-FR-048, CP-FR-049, CP-FR-055)

When all patches are processed, the hub reads the integration branch's head and moves the branch to the new head with one compare-and-swap against the head just read (creating the branch when it does not exist). This is the only moment a rebuild changes a ref that clients read. The job gets `integration_head_sha` (the new head) and `previous_integration_head_sha` (the head replaced; `null` when the branch did not exist).

In the same step, and only when the compare-and-swap wins:

- every patch the run skipped as `merged_upstream`, and that still has that status, is soft-deleted (`parley.patch.delete`, actor `system`, `reason: "merged_upstream"`);
- every patch the run applied and whose status is `conflict` becomes `active` with empty `conflict_files` (`parley.patch.update`, actor `system`, `from: "conflict"`, `to: "active"`, `reason: "rebuild_clean"`);
- the remaining non-deleted patches are renumbered 1..N in their present order.

This also holds for a `continue` run in which other patches conflicted.

A lost compare-and-swap (someone else moved the integration branch after the read) is a retryable failure with reason `ref_moved`; the patch list is as it was and the branch is as the other writer left it.

A run with no applicable patch still publishes: the integration branch moves to the upstream base.

### Push of the integration branch (CP-FR-050)

After a publish, the workspace setting `rebuild_push_integration_branch` is read. When it is true, the hub pushes the integration branch to origin with the origin credentials and force-with-lease against the value it last saw on origin for that branch (`refs/remotes/origin/<integration_branch>`; "must not exist" when it never saw one), within 120 seconds. Success sets `integration_branch_pushed` to true on the job and records the pushed head as the value last seen. A failure (stale lease, origin unreachable, time limit) emits `parley.rebuild.push_failed` with `integration_branch` and `reason` and does not fail the rebuild: the job still completes, `integration_branch_pushed` stays false and the hub's integration branch stays at the new head. When the setting is false, origin is not contacted.

### Stale-input check (CP-FR-051)

After a publish (and the push, when there is one) and after a `fail_fast` conflict, the hub compares its inputs with the present, without fetching:

- a patch listed at the start, and not deleted since, is stale when its branch exists and its tip differs from the recorded `source_sha`;
- upstream is stale when the upstream base resolved now differs from the one the run used.

Stale patches are ignored when `auto_rebuild_after_push` is false; stale upstream is ignored when `auto_rebuild_after_sync` is false. If anything stale remains, the hub queues one follow-up rebuild through the enqueue of package 33, with the job's strategy and fail mode and `submitted_by: "system:followup"`, and emits `parley.rebuild.followup` on the job that ended, with `follow_up_job_id`, `stale_patches` (branch names) and `upstream_stale`. If the enqueue is refused as a duplicate, it is skipped silently: no job, no event. No check is made after a retryable failure, because the job itself runs again and reads fresh inputs.

### Outcome and events (CP-FR-052, §10.8)

A rebuild that published ends `completed`: the four counts are set from `patch_results` (`patches_removed` is the number of merged patches the run soft-deleted), `error` and `conflict` are cleared, and `parley.rebuild.complete` is emitted with `upstream_head_sha`, `integration_head_sha`, `previous_integration_head_sha` and the four counts.

Every failed attempt emits `parley.rebuild.fail` with `reason`, `will_retry` (true when the job waits to retry, false when it is dead-lettered), `retry_count` and, when the failure was a conflict, `conflict`. The job's `error` holds the text of the failure.

Rebuild events have `resource_type: "rebuild"`, the job id as `resource_id`, actor `system`, and the job's session id when it has one. Each is written with the state change it reports. Text that goes into `error` or an event passes through the hub's scrubber first, so that no credential and no URL user information appears in it.

At the end of every attempt, whatever its outcome, the scratch working tree is removed. An attempt begins by discarding a scratch working tree left by an earlier attempt of the same workspace.

### End-to-end flows

**A rebuild that publishes.** A developer runs `parley rebuild submit acme-fork --wait`. `parleyd` queues the job; a worker starts the attempt; the hub fetches upstream, replays the first patch, skips the patch that sync marked `merged_upstream`, replays the third, moves `deploy` to the new head, soft-deletes the merged patch, pushes `deploy` to origin and completes the job. The developer reads the final job record: `completed`, two patches applied, one skipped and removed, `integration_branch_pushed: true`.

**A conflict that the hub learns to resolve.** An agent submits a rebuild after upstream changed a line its patch also changes. The attempt stops at the patch (`fail_fast`): the job is `dead_letter` with a conflict report, the patch is `conflict`, `deploy` has not moved. A developer merges upstream into the patch branch, resolving the conflict, and the dead-lettered job is requeued. The new attempt meets the same conflict, learns the resolution from the merge commit, applies the patch, publishes, and returns the patch to `active`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Contract with the queue of package 33.** This package implements the handler interface of `internal/jobs` as package 33 declares it: a run operation called once per attempt with the job and a context that is cancelled at shutdown, and a settlement hook the queue calls inside the store transaction of each settlement with the job as settled and whether it will be retried. The run operation returns nil (completed), a plain error (retryable), `Permanent(err)` (permanent) or an error with `WithDetail` (the conflict report, which the queue stores as the job's `conflict`); it stores progress and the final counts with `SetResult` while the job is `running`. The hook writes `parley.rebuild.complete`, `parley.rebuild.fail` (with the hook's `will_retry`) and `parley.rebuild.followup` with the state change they report. Nothing in `internal/jobs` is changed by this package.
2. **Order at the end of a run.** Publish with the patch bookkeeping (one store transaction around the compare-and-swap), then the push, then the stale-input check and the follow-up enqueue, then the return to the queue, whose settlement completes the job and calls the hook. The job stays `running` through the push, so that a caller who waits for `completed` reads the final `integration_branch_pushed`, and through the follow-up enqueue, because package 33 accepts a follow-up only for a job that is `running`. If the hub stops between the publish and the completion, the job runs again from the start and publishes again; nothing is lost.
3. **Store and ref together.** The patch bookkeeping is prepared in a store transaction, the compare-and-swap is made, and the transaction commits only when the swap won. A ref and a database cannot commit as one; this order makes a lost swap leave no trace in the patch list.
4. **Scratch working tree.** A detached git working tree of the workspace's repository at `<slug>.git/parley-rebuild/<job id>`. It gives rerere a working tree and adds no ref. One fixed place lets the next attempt, and package 38 at start-up, discard leftovers.
5. **Remembered resolutions are git rerere** with the repository's own `rr-cache`, so they are per workspace and vanish with a reclone, as §10.10 says. Git does not keep the path of a conflict, so the hub records id, path and time in the transactional store (`internal/carrypatch/rerere_entries.go`); `resolved` is read from git. This record is the only one: package 38 lists, counts and forgets these entries through the reads and the removal this package exports, and keeps no file of its own. The entries of a workspace are removed with it (a remover registered with package 14) and after every fresh clone (a post-clone step registered with package 10).
6. **How a resolution is learned.** The PRD says only that "the resolution is learned when a later rebuild sees the same conflict resolved". The hub never edits files itself, so the one place a resolution can be seen is the patch branch: a merge commit there is a conflict the developer resolved. Redoing that merge with rerere on is git's own training method and records exactly the developer's result. It is done only when a conflict remains, and for at most the newest 50 merge commits of the patch, so a clean rebuild costs nothing.
7. **Merge commits made by the hub** carry the hub's landing identity as author as well as committer: there is no original author to keep. With `merge`, a tip already contained in the head under construction is `nothing_to_apply`; the PRD defines that reason for `rebase` only.
8. **Patch status at a conflict** is written when the conflict is found, in both fail modes (state table of §10.3.3), not at the publish. `parley.patch.update` is emitted only when the status changed; a patch that was already `conflict` gets new `conflict_files` and no event.
9. **Bookkeeping follows the present patch list.** A patch whose status a caller changed during the run is treated by its present status at the publish: one no longer `merged_upstream` is not deleted, one no longer `conflict` is not touched. The renumbering after a removal emits no event of its own.
10. **No `parley.git.push` for a move of the integration branch by the hub.** §10.8 says updates of the integration branch also produce the general `parley.git.push` event, but that event's `via` is `git`, `api` or `land` (§5.8) and it is defined for accepted client pushes (GIT-FR-060); no client can push the integration branch. A rebuild's publish is reported by `parley.rebuild.complete`, which carries both heads, and a rollback by `parley.rebuild.rollback` (package 35 records the same decision).
11. **`reason` values of `parley.rebuild.fail`** (the PRD names the field, not its values): `conflict`, `upstream_fetch_failed`, `upstream_unknown`, `git_error`, `timeout`, `shutdown`, `ref_moved`, `workspace_busy`, `workspace_not_ready`, `workspace_archived`. The last three reuse the names of WS-FR-007.
12. **The stale-input check fetches nothing** and compares with the refs as they are. A patch branch that was deleted during the run is not stale, in line with CP-FR-087 (a delete triggers no rebuild).
13. **The push of the integration branch is limited to 120 seconds**, the limit CP-FR-088 gives the mirror; §10.9 calls the push limit fixed without stating it for this push.
14. **Conflict report files** come from the report component of package 26 (`internal/land/`) through a narrow interface of the rebuild, the conflict-file describer, which `internal/hub/` wires. The report builder of this package is exported; the preview of package 35 builds its reports with it, so both are one type.
15. **A lost compare-and-swap** is `ErrRefMoved` of `internal/gitrepo` (package 12). In a rebuild it is the retryable failure reason `ref_moved`; the request routes that meet it (reset to origin in package 32, rollback in package 35) answer `409 ref_moved` with `details.current_sha`.
16. **Git runs through the carry-patch runner of package 31** (`internal/carrypatch/gitrun.go`), which holds the 10-minute limit of CP-FR-093 and cleans error text; its `ErrGitTimeout` is the reason `timeout`. The push uses the lease push operation of package 13 under its 120-second limit, passed to the runner as the shorter deadline.
17. **The follow-up is queued through `RebuildEnqueuer`** (declared by package 31, implemented by package 33) with the follow-up-of id, while the job is still `running`; the event `parley.rebuild.followup` is written in the settlement hook. The upstream fetch of an attempt is `EnsureSetup` of package 31, which also repeats a missing set-up step (CP-FR-005).
18. Project-wide: Go; the `git` command (2.38 or later) run as a subprocess through `internal/gitrepo`, with no git library, a scrubbed environment and no hooks, filters or drivers from repository content (NFR-023); SQLite through `internal/store`; tests with the standard `testing` package, table-driven, with repositories made by `git init` in `t.TempDir()`; a replaceable clock.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Origin**: A registered workspace's remote (`git_url`).
- **Carry-patch workspace**: A workspace that tracks an upstream project and keeps an ordered list of patches on top of it.
- **Upstream**: For a carry-patch workspace, the project it tracks (`upstream_url`).
- **Integration branch**: For a carry-patch workspace, the branch the hub rebuilds as upstream plus the ordered patches.
- **Patch**: A carry-patch entry: a branch with a position in the patch order and a status.
- **Rebuild**: A durable job that recreates the integration branch.
- **Durable job**: Background work that is recorded before its request returns, survives restarts and is retried with backoff. Rebuilds are the only durable jobs (§10).
- **Conflict report**: The structured description of why a rebase could not be done: files, kinds, and the landed changes involved.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number.
- **Upstream base**: The commit every rebuild starts from: the head of the upstream's default branch as of the last upstream fetch.
- **Patch branch**: The branch that holds a patch's commits.
- **Head under construction**: The commit a run has built so far: the upstream base, then the result of each applied patch.
- **Attempt**: One execution of a rebuild job by a worker. A job that fails with a retryable failure gets another attempt.
- **Remembered resolution**: A recorded way a conflict was resolved, which the hub replays when the same conflict appears again (git rerere).
- **Scratch working tree**: The temporary working tree a run builds in; no ref points to it.
- **Stale input**: A patch tip or an upstream base that changed after the run read it.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Start an attempt: workspace state, upstream fetch and upstream base

**Rationale:** Every rebuild starts from the upstream as it is now, and a workspace that cannot be rebuilt must end the job in the way that says whether trying again can help.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a worker starts an attempt of a rebuild job whose carry-patch workspace is in status ready, THE parleyd SHALL fetch upstream with the upstream credentials into refs/remotes/upstream/* without tags, resolve the upstream base as the head of the upstream's default branch, store it on the job as upstream_head_sha and empty the job's patch_results
   → the job record has upstream_head_sha equal to the 40-character head of the upstream's default branch after the fetch and patch_results []; refs/remotes/upstream/<branch> equals each upstream branch; no ref under refs/tags/ is created; the fetch used UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT when set, else UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME with UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD, else the origin credential of the workspace
   Check: integration
   - setup: the rebuild fixture, built in this file and reused by every test of the package: an upstream bare repository, an origin bare repository and the hub's bare repository made with git in t.TempDir(); a carry-patch workspace record in status ready with integration_branch deploy in a real store in t.TempDir(); patches registered in the store with their branches in the hub repository; a queued rebuild job claimed for one attempt; a fixed clock; a recording event emitter; the landing identity Parley <parley@localhost>; hooks the test can set to run code before a given patch and before the publish
   - setup: for the credential table: a recording fetcher in place of the git fetch
   ```
   in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_FetchesUpstreamAndRecordsBase: add commit U2 and tag v9 to upstream after the workspace was set up; run one attempt; assert job.upstream_head_sha == U2; assert ref refs/remotes/upstream/main == U2; assert no ref refs/tags/v9 in the hub repository; assert job.patch_results == [] for a job record that carried results of an earlier attempt. Then a table over the secrets {UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT set -> resolver returns the token, only UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME and UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD -> that pair, none -> the origin credential}: assert the credential the recording fetcher received
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] WHEN the upstream's default branch is unknown after the fetch and upstream has a branch named like the workspace's default_branch, THE parleyd SHALL use the head of that upstream branch as the upstream base
   → the job's upstream_head_sha equals the head of refs/remotes/upstream/<default_branch of the workspace>
   Check: integration

   → the patch result has status success and new_head_sha equal to the head under construction after the patch; the commits between the previous head under construction and new_head_sha are as many as the replayed commits, in the same order, each with the original author name, author email, author date and message and with committer [land].committer_name <[land].committer_email>; the first patch is applied onto the upstream base and each later patch onto the new_head_sha of the last applied patch

### REQ-4: Report a conflicting patch and follow the fail mode

**Rationale:** A team must learn which patch stopped applying, on which files and against what, in the same form a landing conflict has, and must be able to choose between an unchanged branch and a branch without the broken patch.

Run a second attempt of a new job: assert no further parley.patch.update for p1

   → after a run that left a.txt in conflict, the workspace's remembered-resolution entries contain {id: the rerere id, path: "a.txt", resolved: false, recorded_at: the clock's time}; a second run that meets the same conflict adds no second entry; another workspace with the same conflict has no entry from this workspace and replays none of its resolutions

   → when the patch branch holds a merge of the upstream base that resolved the conflict, the patch result is success and the file in new_head_sha has the content the merge commit gave it; the entry of that conflict has resolved true and recorded_at the time of the learning; a later run on a workspace whose patch branch no longer holds the merge commit, meeting the same conflict, also ends success; a patch whose merge commits do not resolve the conflict is recorded as conflict

### REQ-6: Publish the new head in one step with the patch list changes

**Rationale:** Readers of the integration branch must never see a half-built branch, and the patch list must not say a merged patch is gone or a conflict is over unless the branch that proves it is the one published.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] WHEN every patch of a run is processed and the workspace is ready, THE parleyd SHALL read the head of the integration branch and move the branch to the new head with one compare-and-swap against the head just read, creating the branch when it does not exist, and store integration_head_sha and previous_integration_head_sha on the job
   → refs/heads/<integration_branch> equals the head under construction after the last patch; job.integration_head_sha equals it; job.previous_integration_head_sha equals the head the branch had immediately before, or null when the branch did not exist; no other ref under refs/heads/, refs/tags/ or refs/parley/ differs from before the attempt
   Check: integration
   - setup: the rebuild fixture of internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go with two active patches
   ```
   in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_publish_test.go, TestRebuild_PublishMovesOnlyTheIntegrationBranch, a table over {deploy exists at H0 -> previous == H0; deploy does not exist -> previous == null and the branch is created}: before = git for-each-ref refs/heads refs/tags refs/parley; run one attempt; assert head of deploy == last new_head_sha == job.integration_head_sha; assert job.previous_integration_head_sha; assert for-each-ref after differs from before in refs/heads/deploy only
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] IF the integration branch is moved by another writer between the read of its head and the compare-and-swap, THEN THE parleyd SHALL end the attempt as a retryable failure, leave the integration branch as the other writer left it and leave every patch record as it was before the publish
   → the attempt's outcome is a retryable failure with reason ref_moved; the integration branch equals the other writer's commit; no patch was soft-deleted, renumbered or returned to active, and no parley.patch.delete, parley.patch.update with reason rebuild_clean or parley.rebuild.complete event was written
   Check: integration

   in internal/carrypatch/rebuild_publish_test.go, TestRebuild_LostCompareAndSwapIsRetryable: hook between the read and the swap moves deploy to commit W; out = run one attempt; assert out.kind == retryable and out.reason == 'ref_moved'; assert head of deploy == W; assert the merged patch still has status merged_upstream and its position, the conflict patch still has status conflict; assert the emitter holds no parley.patch.delete, no rebuild_clean update and no parley.rebuild.complete
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] WHEN the compare-and-swap of the publish wins, THE parleyd SHALL in the same step soft-delete every patch the run skipped as merged_upstream that still has that status, set every patch the run applied whose status is conflict to active with empty conflict_files, renumber the remaining non-deleted patches 1..N in their present order, and emit one event per removed and per returned patch, also when other patches of a continue run conflicted
   → each removed patch has status deleted, position null and deleted_at the clock's time, with one event parley.patch.delete (actor system, metadata {branch_name, reason: "merged_upstream"}); each returned patch has status active and conflict_files [], with one event parley.patch.update (actor system, metadata {branch_name, changed: ["status"], from: "conflict", to: "active", reason: "rebuild_clean"}); the non-deleted patches hold positions 1..N without gaps in their former order; a patch that a caller changed from merged_upstream to another status during the run is not deleted; a reader that sees the new integration head also sees these patch changes

1. [REQ-6.4] WHEN a run has no applicable patch, because every patch is disabled, merged_upstream, without a branch or has nothing to apply, or because the workspace has no patch, THE parleyd SHALL publish all the same, moving the integration branch to the upstream base

### REQ-7: Push the integration branch to origin when the workspace asks for it

**Rationale:** Teams deploy from their own copy of the repository; the rebuilt branch must reach it without overwriting what someone else put there, and a push problem must not undo a good rebuild.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHERE the workspace setting rebuild_push_integration_branch, read after the publish, is true, THE parleyd SHALL push the integration branch to origin with the origin credentials of the workspace and force-with-lease against the value the hub last saw on origin for that branch, within 120 seconds, and on success set integration_branch_pushed and record the pushed head as the value last seen
   → origin's integration branch equals job.integration_head_sha; the completed job has integration_branch_pushed true; refs/remotes/origin/<integration_branch> in the hub equals the pushed head; when the hub never saw the branch on origin the lease is that origin has no such branch; a setting changed to true while the attempt ran is honoured
   Check: integration

   - setup: the real durable queue of internal/jobs with the rebuild handler registered

   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] IF the push of the integration branch fails, because origin's branch is not at the value the hub last saw, origin cannot be reached, or the push exceeds 120 seconds, THEN THE parleyd SHALL emit parley.rebuild.push_failed, complete the rebuild all the same and leave the hub's integration branch at the new head
   → one event parley.rebuild.push_failed with resource_type rebuild, resource_id the job id, actor system and metadata {integration_branch, reason} whose reason carries no credential and no URL user information; the job is completed with integration_branch_pushed false; the hub's integration branch equals integration_head_sha; origin's branch is as the other writer left it; refs/remotes/origin/<integration_branch> is unchanged

**Rationale:** Triggers that arrive while a rebuild runs are skipped; the check at the end is what guarantees that a skipped trigger loses nothing.

### REQ-9: Record the outcome of every attempt and clean up

**Rationale:** The job record and its events are how a waiting caller, an operator and a webhook subscriber learn what a rebuild did; an attempt that leaves files behind would fill the disk one retry at a time.

   Check: integration

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer rebuilds a carry-patch workspace and the new integration branch reaches origin

1. **developer** runs parley rebuild submit acme-fork --wait on a carry-patch workspace with three patches, the second marked merged_upstream, and rebuild_push_integration_branch true
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/acme-fork/rebuild and then polls GET /api/v1/workspaces/acme-fork/rebuilds/:id
3. **parleyd** queues the job, and a worker starts the attempt by calling the rebuild handler
4. **parleyd** fetches upstream, resolves the upstream base and records the tip of every patch branch
5. **parleyd** replays the first patch in a scratch working tree, skips the merged patch, replays the third, and stores the results after each
6. **parleyd** moves deploy to the new head by compare-and-swap and, in the same step, soft-deletes the merged patch and renumbers the others
7. **parleyd** pushes deploy to origin with force-with-lease
8. **origin** accepts the push and now holds deploy at the new head
9. **parleyd** finds no stale input, completes the job and emits parley.rebuild.complete
10. **parley CLI** prints the final job record and exits 0
11. **developer** reads status completed, patches_applied 2, patches_skipped 1, patches_removed 1 and integration_branch_pushed true

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its real router, authentication and access middleware, the durable job queue of internal/jobs and its worker, the rebuild handler of internal/carrypatch, internal/gitrepo running the git binary, with git rerere, the conflict report component of internal/land, the SQLite store of internal/store, the event log of internal/event, an upstream and an origin git repository served to the hub by internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest, the parley CLI command tree of internal/cli with its real HTTP client

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process as the end-to-end tests of package 01 start it, against a data directory in t.TempDir()
- an upstream repository and an origin repository cloned from it, served by the test origin helper; upstream then gains one commit
- the carry-patch workspace acme-fork created through POST /api/v1/workspaces and cloned; three patch branches pushed to origin before the clone and registered through POST /api/v1/workspaces/acme-fork/patches; the second patch set to merged_upstream through PATCH; the setting rebuild_push_integration_branch set to true

**End state:**

- the command exits 0 and its stdout is a job record with status completed, patches_applied 2, patches_skipped 1, patches_removed 1 and integration_branch_pushed true
- deploy in the hub's repository and deploy in the origin repository both equal the job's integration_head_sha, whose history is the upstream head followed by the commits of patches one and three
- GET /api/v1/workspaces/acme-fork/patches lists two patches at positions 1 and 2
- the event log holds parley.rebuild.complete for the job and parley.patch.delete for the merged patch

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_PublishesAndPushes: out, code = run the CLI with rebuild submit acme-fork --wait --poll-interval 100ms; assert code == 0; job = json(out); assert job.status == 'completed' and the three counts and job.integration_branch_pushed; assert git rev-parse deploy in the hub repository == git rev-parse deploy in the origin repository == job.integration_head_sha; assert the subjects of git log upstream_head..deploy are the subjects of patches one and three; assert len(GET patches .items) == 2; assert GET /api/v1/events/log holds one parley.rebuild.complete with resource_id job.id and one parley.patch.delete
```

### PATH-2: An agent's rebuild stops at a conflict and a later attempt learns the resolution from the patch branch

1. **agent** sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/acme-fork/rebuild after upstream changed a line that the patch on branch feature/a also changes
2. **parleyd** queues the job with fail_mode fail_fast and starts the attempt
3. **parleyd** fetches upstream, replays the patch, finds a.txt in conflict with no remembered resolution, records the conflict and marks the patch conflict
4. **parleyd** dead-letters the job with the conflict report, emits parley.rebuild.fail with will_retry false, and leaves deploy where it was
5. **agent** reads GET /api/v1/workspaces/acme-fork/rebuilds/:id and finds the conflict report naming a.txt
6. **developer** merges upstream into feature/a with a.txt resolved, so that the patch branch in the hub holds the merge commit, and sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/acme-fork/rebuilds/:id/requeue
7. **parleyd** starts a new attempt, meets the same conflict, redoes the merge commit of the patch branch, records its content of a.txt as the resolution and replays the patch with it
8. **parleyd** moves deploy to the new head, returns the patch to active and completes the job
9. **agent** reads the job as completed and a.txt on deploy with the developer's resolution

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with its real router, authentication and access middleware, the durable job queue of internal/jobs and its worker, the rebuild handler of internal/carrypatch, internal/gitrepo running the git binary, with git rerere, the conflict report component of internal/land, the SQLite store of internal/store, the event log of internal/event, an upstream and an origin git repository served to the hub by internal/gitrepo/gitrepotest

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process as the end-to-end tests of package 01 start it, against a data directory in t.TempDir()
- the carry-patch workspace acme-fork with one registered patch on branch feature/a whose single commit changes line 3 of a.txt; the default settings (rebase, fail_fast) with auto_rebuild_after_push false so that only the test queues rebuilds
- upstream gains a commit that changes line 3 of a.txt differently
- between the two attempts the test writes the merge commit to feature/a directly in the hub's bare repository with git, standing in for a push

**End state:**

- after the first attempt the job is dead_letter, its conflict has files [a.txt] with kind content, the patch has status conflict and deploy is at the head it had before
- after the requeue the job is completed with patches_applied 1, the patch has status active with conflict_files [], and a.txt on deploy has the content of the developer's merge commit
- the event log holds parley.rebuild.fail (reason conflict, will_retry false), then parley.rebuild.complete for the same job

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/rebuild_test.go, TestRebuild_ConflictThenLearnedResolution: before = rev-parse deploy; id = POST rebuild .json.id; wait until GET rebuilds/id .status == 'dead_letter'; assert .conflict.files[0].path == 'a.txt' and .conflict.files[0].kind == 'content'; assert GET patches/pid .status == 'conflict' and rev-parse deploy == before; write merge commit M (parents: feature/a, upstream head; a.txt resolved to R) to refs/heads/feature/a in the hub repository; POST rebuilds/id/requeue; wait until status == 'completed'; assert .patches_applied == 1; assert GET patches/pid .status == 'active' and .conflict_files == []; assert git show deploy:a.txt == R; assert the event log has parley.rebuild.fail then parley.rebuild.complete with resource_id id
```


# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/carrypatch/... ./internal/gitrepo/... ./internal/jobs/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `26` — rebuild conflicts take their file entries from its conflict report component in internal/land
- `33` — runs as the handler of the durable rebuild jobs that package queues: its worker calls the run operation once per attempt and the settlement hook inside each settlement, its job record holds the result this package writes, and its enqueue queues the follow-up
- `52` — emits parley.rebuild.* and the rebuild-caused parley.patch.* events through its event component, in the transaction of the state change
- `13` — pushes the integration branch to origin with the lease push operation it adds to internal/gitrepo
- `14` — registers the remover of a workspace's remembered-resolution entries with the removers of owned data it declares

## Tasks

### 1. Start an attempt: check the workspace, fetch upstream and resolve the upstream base (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-1.1, REQ-1.2, REQ-1.3, REQ-1.4, REQ-1.5

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go and confirm they fail; build the shared rebuild fixture there: an upstream, an origin and a hub bare repository made with git in t.TempDir(), a carry-patch workspace record in status ready with integration_branch deploy in a real store, helpers that register patches and create their branches, a rebuild job claimed for one attempt, a fixed clock, a recording event emitter, the landing identity, and hooks that run test code before a given patch and before the publish
- 1.2 In internal/carrypatch add the rebuild handler: one operation that runs one attempt of a rebuild job and returns an outcome value that is completed, a retryable failure or a permanent failure, each failure with a reason word, a text and, for a conflict, the conflict report; library code returns the outcome and never ends the process
- 1.3 Declare what the handler needs as narrow interfaces so tests can replace them: the workspace reader, the patch store, the job record writer, the upstream fetcher with its credential resolver, the settings reader, the clock, the event emitter, the conflict-file describer, the pusher and the enqueuer (the interface RebuildEnqueuer of package 31)
- 1.4 At the start of an attempt read the workspace: archived ends the attempt as a permanent failure with reason workspace_archived and failed with workspace_not_ready; pending or cloning ends it as a retryable failure with reason workspace_busy; a workspace that no longer exists ends it with nothing written and no event; none of these starts a fetch
- 1.5 On a ready workspace start with an empty patch_results, then run EnsureSetup of package 31, which fetches upstream into refs/remotes/upstream/* without tags with the upstream credential resolution of that package (UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT, else UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME with UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD, else the origin credential of the workspace) and repeats a missing set-up step; a failed fetch step is a retryable failure with reason upstream_fetch_failed, and a failure of another set-up step is logged and does not end the attempt
- 1.6 Resolve the upstream base with UpstreamBase of package 31: the head of the upstream's default branch, else the upstream branch named like the workspace's default_branch; store it on the job as upstream_head_sha; when neither resolves end the attempt as a retryable failure with reason upstream_unknown
- 1.7 Run every git operation of the rebuild, in this and the later tasks, through the carry-patch git runner of package 31 (internal/carrypatch/gitrun.go), and read the integration branch name from the job, where package 33 captured it through IntegrationBranch of package 31

### 2. Replay the patches by rebase in a scratch working tree and publish the head (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2.1, REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, REQ-3.6, REQ-6.1

**Steps:**

- 2.1 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/gitrepo/scratch_test.go, internal/carrypatch/rebuild_test.go, internal/carrypatch/rebuild_strategy_test.go and internal/carrypatch/rebuild_publish_test.go and confirm they fail
- 2.2 In internal/gitrepo add the scratch working tree: a detached git working tree of a bare repository at <repository>/parley-rebuild/<job id>, checked out at a given commit, created without adding or moving any ref, with an operation that removes it and its administrative entry; git runs with the wrapper's scrubbed environment, with hooks off and without filters or merge drivers from repository content
- 2.3 Add to the scratch working tree the replay of one commit onto its HEAD: it keeps the commit's author, author date and message, sets the committer to an identity passed in by the caller and the committer date from the clock, and reports one of three results: applied (with the new commit), dropped because the commit's change is already present (HEAD unchanged), or conflicted (with the conflicted paths)
- 2.4 After the upstream base is resolved, list the non-deleted patches of the workspace in position order and read the tip of each patch branch once into source_sha (null when the branch does not exist); pass only these commits to every later step
- 2.5 Start the head under construction at the upstream base; for a patch applied with strategy rebase take the commits reachable from source_sha and not from the upstream base, oldest first, leave out commits with more than one parent, and replay the others; the patch result is success with new_head_sha the head under construction after the patch
- 2.6 Take the committer from the landing identity of the server configuration ([land].committer_name and [land].committer_email) and pass it explicitly to every git call that creates a commit
- 2.7 Publish: read the head of the integration branch named on the job, and move the branch to the head under construction with one compare-and-swap of internal/gitrepo against the head just read, creating the branch when it does not exist; store integration_head_sha and previous_integration_head_sha (null when the branch did not exist) on the job
- 2.8 Change no ref other than refs/remotes/upstream/* before the publish and only the integration branch at the publish

### 5. Report a conflicting patch, follow the fail mode, and clean up after every attempt (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-4, REQ-9.4

**Depends on:** 3, 4

**Steps:**

- 5.1 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/carrypatch/rebuild_conflict_test.go and internal/carrypatch/rebuild_outcome_test.go and confirm they fail
- 5.2 When a replayed commit or a merge reports conflicted paths, undo the patch: abort the operation in the scratch working tree and return its HEAD to the head under construction before the patch, so that none of the patch's commits stays in what the run goes on with
- 5.3 In one store transaction set the patch's status to conflict and its conflict_files to the conflicted paths in ascending order, and, only when the status was not conflict before, emit parley.patch.update (resource_type patch, resource_id the patch id, actor system, metadata branch_name, changed ["status"], from, to conflict, reason rebuild_conflict)
- 5.4 Build the conflict report in one exported builder, which the preview of package 35 also calls so that both reports are one type: patch_id; target_sha the head under construction before the patch; head_sha the source_sha; base_sha the merge base of source_sha and target_sha; commit_sha the commit that did not apply, or source_sha with strategy merge; landed_changes [] and change null; files from the conflict-file describer for the conflicted paths, ours being the file in target_sha and theirs the file in commit_sha, each with landed_by []
- 5.5 Declare the conflict-file describer as a narrow interface of the rebuild that returns the file entries of the conflict report of package 26 (path, kind, base, ours, theirs) for a target commit, a patch commit and a list of paths; the real one is the conflict report component of internal/land
- 5.6 Record the patch result as conflict with the same conflict_files and the report, and store progress
- 5.7 With fail_mode fail_fast stop the run there: process no later patch, do not publish, and return a permanent failure with reason conflict, the report, and a text that names the patch's branch and the number of conflicted files
- 5.8 With fail_mode continue go on with the next patch from the head under construction before the conflicting patch, and publish at the end
- 5.9 Every git operation of a run has the runner's deadline of 10 minutes (a value tests can shorten), after which the runner kills the git process and its children; return a retryable failure with reason timeout for the runner's ErrGitTimeout, shutdown when the attempt's context was cancelled, and git_error for any other git failure that is not a conflict; in these cases record no result for the patch in work, change no patch and do not publish
- 5.10 Remove the scratch working tree before the attempt returns on every path out of it (completed, either kind of failure, cancelled context), and at the start of an attempt remove every entry left under <repository>/parley-rebuild/ and prune the repository's working-tree list, through one exported operation of internal/gitrepo/scratch.go that package 38 also calls for every workspace when the hub starts

**Criteria:** REQ-5

- 6.6 Learn from the patch branch when paths are still unresolved: list the commits with exactly two parents that are reachable from source_sha and not from the upstream base, newest first, 50 at most; for each, in the scratch working tree, check out the first parent and merge the second with rerere on; where that merge conflicts, write the merge commit's own content for each conflicted path, let git record it as the resolution, and set recorded_at of the entry to the clock's time; then return the working tree to the head under construction
- 6.7 After learning, replay the commit that did not apply once more; when it now applies, go on with the patch; when paths are still unresolved, treat the patch as conflicting as task 5 does; learn at most once per patch per attempt
- 6.8 Keep the conflict report and conflict_files to the paths still unresolved after the replay of resolutions

**Criteria:** REQ-9.1, REQ-9.2, REQ-9.3

The run operation returns nil for a completed outcome, a plain error for a retryable failure, Permanent(err) for a permanent one and WithDetail(err, report) when the failure carries a conflict report; it keeps the outcome of the attempt it just ran (reason, text, counts, follow-up) for the hook, which the queue calls inside the transaction of the settlement
- 8.4 On a completed outcome store, with SetResult of internal/jobs before the run operation returns, the result document with the counts over patch_results (success, skipped and conflict results, and patches_removed from the publish); the queue's settlement clears error and conflict; in the settlement hook emit parley.rebuild.complete with metadata upstream_head_sha, integration_head_sha, previous_integration_head_sha and the four counts
